Test suites must not inherit from base test classes.

What The Standard says

“Vertical Entanglement” — The Standard rejects local base components because inherited shared behavior creates hidden vertical coupling and a single point of failure. Test base classes introduce the same obscured dependency. read it here.
“Unit Tests” — Canonical tests construct their subject and dependencies within the test suite. Requiring standalone suites keeps every test's setup locally discoverable. read it here.

Why it matters

Inherited test bases hide setup and behaviour outside the suite a reviewer is reading. Keeping tests composition-based and self-contained makes dependencies explicit and prevents shared mutable fixtures from coupling otherwise independent suites.

Bad code example

// Violates STXTEST002: Test suites must not inherit from base test classes.
class StudentServiceTests : ServiceTestsBase { }

Good code example

// Follows STXTEST002
class StudentServiceTests { }
